title: Viva Insights: agent query for custom agent adoption reporting in the analyst workbench
summary: The roadmap details, query outputs, licensing prerequisites and documented access control are supported. Minor corrections should complete the admin route, cite the cmdlet reference and clarify the Advanced analysis policy's documented reach. The checklist also names controls that have no table rows.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access reaches the advanced analysis policy management page.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. ... Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. ... Select Create a policy.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and its rendered copy to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > Off > Apply access settings to > Everyone'. The existing route is correct but stops at the policy management page.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId AdvancedInsights -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone disables advanced analysis tenant-wide.
claims.quote:
Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy
    -FeatureId <String>
    -IsFeatureEnabled <Boolean>
    -ModuleId <String>
    -Name <String>
    [-Confirm]
    [-Everyone]
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchange/add-vivamodulefeaturepolicy to sources. The existing cited advanced-analysis page supplies VivaInsights, AdvancedInsights and the disabling example; this additional reference verifies the actual parameter syntax and boolean value.
